offsets.name: FONT_WIDTHS
offsets.evidence: width(c) is at font+0x90+4*(c-0x20) in 1.0.116 (CFont::CFont 0x0050E750: ebp=esi+0x90 for c=0x20..0xFE); the ES and PT-BR constructors store it at font+0x10+4*c from c=0 (lea ebx,[esi+0x10], add ebx,4) - the same address for every c the host writes

offsets.name: FONT_FIRST_CHAR
offsets.evidence: the first character the host measures; width(0x20) is at font+0x90 in 1.0.116 and at font+0x10+4*0x20 in ES and PT-BR (same address); lower characters are not read

offsets.name: FONT_END_CHAR
offsets.evidence: the host stops before 0xFF (1.0.116 stores 0x20..0xFE, jb 0xFF); ES and PT-BR store 0..0xFF (jbe 0xFF), so every character the host reads exists in both layouts

offsets.name: BOX_SUB_EXTENTS
offsets.evidence: sub-box i keeps six floats at box+0xD8+0x18*i: 0x004E9780 and 0x004EACCB (BoxBox) read [i*0x18+0xDC] and [+0xE0] (y, z of the first triple) and [+0xE4]..[+0xEC] (the second), and 0x004DC0B0/0x004DE3A0/0x004DF7D0 take the second triple with lea [ebx+i*0x18+0xE4]; those functions are byte-identical in the ES executable. 1.0.116 has no access with displacement 0xD8 itself, so x is proven only through its triple

offsets.name: FONT_WIDTH_BASE
offsets.evidence: width(c) is at font+0x10+4*c in ES and PT-BR (CFont::CFont, lea ebx,[esi+0x10] then add ebx,4 for c=0..0xFF) and at font+0x90+4*(c-0x20) = font+0x10+4*c in 1.0.116 for c >= 0x20; the host reads printable characters
